predecessors.note: Infobox predecessor: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia. The Mamluks took Adana and Tarsus in 1359 and Sis in 1375 and authorised the Turkmen emirate to administer Cilicia.

land.text: Cilicia, the beylik incorporated by Selim I

successors.note: Infobox: protectorate of the Ottoman Empire 1517-1608; the beys held the sanjak of Adana hereditarily to 1608.

capitals.name: Adana
capitals.note: Infobox capital Adana; 'The Ramadanids made Adana their center of power' after the Mamluk takeover of Cilicia. Their first settlement in 1352 was Camili, south of Çaldağı, and Adana itself was Armenian until the Mamluks took it in 1359.

rulers.name: Ramazan Bey
rulers.note: The page's list gives '1353' only and nothing for 1353-1378.

rulers.name: Selim
rulers.note: The list continues with Mahmud II (1516-1517) and Qubadh (1517-1520) as Ottoman protectorate rulers, outside this state's life.

correction.text: the Yüreğir land south-east of Adana

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates the emirate from 1352 (infobox 'Established: 1352'; first settlement Camili south of Çaldağı, the Yüreğir Turkmens 'southeast of Adana'); Cliopatria starts in 1385. Adana itself fell to the Mamluks in 1359 and its plain was authorised to the emirate only after 1375, so the early core is a modest radius.

correction.text: the Cilician plain administered by the emirate under Mamluk protection

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 1375 'the fall of Sis to the Mamluks, followed by the fortress of Gaban' ended the Armenian kingdom; the Mamluks then 'authorized the Türkmen emirate to administer Cilicia but took direct control of Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar, and Sis' (Ramadanid page). Cliopatria's 1385 shape projected back ten years; it is generous, because it covers Tarsus and the Kozan hills the Mamluks kept.

24,029 km2 (Adana 72%, Mersin 51%, Osmaniye 73%) against the infobox's 15,000 km2: ratio 1.6, inside the factor of two. The shape includes Tarsus and the Sis hills which the page puts under direct Mamluk control; the Mamluk dossier treats the whole as a protectorate from c. 1385.
24,029 km2, the same 86 grid cells as 1385. Unverified: page budget; the page dates no frontier change after 1375 (only a Karaman-allied rising and the battle of Belen, undated).
24,453 km2 (+1.8%): two more grid cells than 1402 (88 against 86), a boundary-level change; no event on the pages opened explains it. Unverified: page budget.
24,477 km2 (+0.1%): the same 88 grid cells as 1450; no event on any page; the Karamanid page has Ramazanoglu Ali Bey capturing Tarsus without a year. Unverified: page budget.

24,477 km2, the same 88 grid cells. The shape runs to 1515; the Ramadanid page dates Selim I's incorporation to 1516 and the protectorate to 1517 (the Ottoman-Mamluk war ran 1516 - 22 January 1517), so the last Ramadanid year is 1516.

region.text: the Yüreğir land south-east of Adana

ledger.note: 1352: Ramazan Beg settles the Yüreğir Turkmens south of Çaldağı (first settlement Camili) and, visiting Cairo the same year, is 'assented by the Sultan' to found a frontier Turkmen emirate in Cilicia. Infobox 'Established: 1352'; protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate 1352-c. 1397.

Page silent on the date of the handover: after the Mamluks took Sis in 1375 ('ending three centuries of Armenian rule') they 'authorized the Türkmen emirate to administer Cilicia' while keeping Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar and Sis. Placed at 1375; the Mamluk dossier has the protectorate over the plain from c. 1385, Cliopatria's first shape year.

1516: Selim I incorporates the beylik into the Ottoman Empire after conquering the Mamluk state ('In 1516, Selim I incorporated the beylik'); the infobox begins the Ottoman protectorate in 1517. A 'Ramazanoglu Bey' is listed killed on the Mamluk side of the war (Ottoman-Mamluk War page).

1516: the independent emirate ends when Selim I incorporates it; the dynasty keeps the sanjak of Adana as an Ottoman protectorate (1517-1608). Cliopatria ends the row in 1515; the Ottoman dossier has its gain in 1515.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of Armenian Cilicia
wars.outcome: Mamluks invade Cilicia again in 1343-44, take Adana and Tarsus in 1359 and Sis and Gaban in 1375, ending the Armenian kingdom; the Ramadanid Turkmen emirate administers the plain under Mamluk protection.
wars.note: The Cilicia page does not mention 1359 (the Ramadanid page does) nor the Ramadanids beyond the infobox.

wars.name: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1516-1517)
wars.outcome: Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516) and Ridaniya (24 January 1517) give the Ottomans Syria and Egypt; Selim I incorporates the Ramadanid beylik in 1516; a Ramazanoglu Bey is listed killed on the Mamluk side.
wars.note: The war page names no Ramadanid submission, Adana or Cilicia.

certainty.note: A frontier emirate of the Cilician plain under Mamluk protection to c. 1397 and between Mamluks, Karamanids and Dulkadir afterwards; no treaty frontier on any page.

notes:
Four pages opened (state article, Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, Ottoman-Mamluk War, Karamanids; the last cited only in sources). Page budget up to 5.
Cliopatria problems: the five shapes are the same 24,000 km2 shape (differences under 2%); the row is dated 1385-1515, the page has the emirate from 1352 and the independent beylik to 1516 (Ottoman protectorate 1517-1608, with the line holding the sanjak of Adana to 1608). The infobox area (15,000 km2) is 1.6 times smaller than the shape; the shape includes Tarsus and the Kozan hills, which the page puts under direct Mamluk control.
Vassal relations in which this state is the vassal belong to the overlord: Mamluk protectorate 1352 - c. 1397 (infobox; the Mamluk dossier has vassal_start c. 1385 and vassal_end c. 1397), 'de facto independent c. 1397-1517', Ottoman protectorate from 1517. Disagreement to settle: Ottoman dossier (ottoman-empire) has gain ramadanid-emirate in 1515, this page 1516.
Not settled: the dates of Ibrahim Bey's alliance with Karaman, the battle of Belen (a Mamluk army raided, Ibrahim defeated it and captured Temur Bey) and the Aleppo amir Yilboga's capture of Misis, all undated on the Ramadanid page; Tarsus changing hands among Ramadanids, Karamanids and Mamluks (Karamanids page: 'Ramazanoglu Ali Bey captured Tarsus', undated); relations with Dulkadir (not mentioned by the Ramadanid page); the rulers between Ramazan Bey (1353) and Ibrahim I (1378).
The Kingdom of Cyprus (a neighbour 1385-1486 in Cliopatria) is not mentioned on any page opened.
Gazetteer: every name resolves.
